A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISMM-Bench and contain readable main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices A–H. Their content can be matched reliably despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 21 LMMs, an eight-participant human study, and resolution and chain-of-thought ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports updated benchmark evaluations, retains the human study, and adds open-ended judging results and a random-subset simulation in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The six-stage construction pipeline, three principal benchmark tasks, Evidence–Claim and Target–Action JSON representations, and task-generation procedures remain unchanged. The added open-ended experiment evaluates an alternative format without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The evaluated corpus expands from ICLR 2025 to ICLR 2024 and 2025 papers. Figure 9 adds figure–algorithm and table–equation inconsistencies, and Appendix C.3 evaluates open-ended identification. These extend coverage within the retained AI-paper domain and three principal tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds open-ended generation with LLM-as-a-judge scoring as an alternative comparison to MCQ evaluation, using Gemini, GPT-5, and GLM judges. The main 21-LMM roster and existing natural-language versus JSON comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 increases Ident and Remedy samples from 262 to 384 and Match samples from 135 to 192. New protocols include eight-model open-ended evaluation with three judges, Likert-5 scores and context controls, plus 40-item subset resampling. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Core inference settings remain unchanged; Appendix D.4.4 inconsistently retains the old dataset counts.

E4.justification: v3 adds two substantive benchmark-validity analyses: sensitivity of open-ended scoring to judge and context (Appendix C.3, Table 5), and representativeness of the human-study subset (Appendix E.2, Table 6). The resolution ablation remains unchanged; the existing chain-of-thought analysis is relocated and its results updated.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 newly reports a 100-trial simulation sampling 40 instances, with means and 75th percentiles for two models under two context conditions. This adds sampling-variability reporting without documenting additional repeated LMM inference runs or confidence intervals for the main results.

E6.justification: Most Table 1 scores are replaced for the expanded benchmark: GPT-5 high and Gemini 2.5 Pro previously tied at 54.2%, whereas v3 reports 53.9% and 52.8%. These are different-dataset results, not same-setting performance changes. Table 3, chain-of-thought results, and dataset distributions also change, and Tables 5–6 add findings. Tables 2 and 4 retain their results.

T1.justification: The Visual Reliance Ratio definition in Equation 1 is unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new evaluation and simulation introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The four central contributions remain the reviewer-sourced dataset, three-task benchmark, JSON debiasing, and 21-LMM evaluation. The conclusions about weak scientific reasoning, long-context difficulties, and linguistic shortcuts remain intact; dataset counts and headline scores are updated.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly argues that judge disagreement, nondeterminism, and model-family preferences favor MCQ evaluation. Appendix E.2 interprets the comparatively easy human-study subset as making the human advantage conservative. Existing reasoning-mechanism explanations and domain and submission-selection limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The cover replaces direct code and dataset links with a project-site link. Appendix A removes local dataset-viewer launch instructions and the release-upon-acceptance statement; Appendix B adds the ICLR 2024 source and license information. Hardware, inference software, decoding settings, and existing prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether underlying resource availability changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds MT-Bench and AlpacaEval references to support the judge-bias discussion and supplies explicit VLM references where Section 2 previously contained unresolved citations. Its positioning against scientific QA and synthetic-inconsistency benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The chain-of-thought analysis moves from Appendix C.2 into new Section 4.3, shifting the user study to Section 4.4. Appendix E gains subsections, Appendix A is shortened, and local wording and cross-references are corrected. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–6, redraws Figure 9 for 15 categories, restores the truncated ending of Figure 6, and adjusts table widths and placement. The pipeline diagrams, qualitative examples, prompts, and interface illustrations are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The additional real-error coverage and new judge-sensitivity and subset-variability analyses strengthen the evidence supporting the benchmark and its evaluation choices. The gains are limited by incomplete reporting of the open-ended experiment, including missing sample counts and judge prompts, and unreconciled old dataset counts in Appendix D.4.4. Overall, v3 provides a modestly better-supported paper.
